title: Scoped security acceptance and operational runbook for encrypted private deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket codifies the acceptance criteria and operator runbooks required to onboard enterprise customers to Redwood Private with SSO (SAML/OIDC), RBAC, audit logging, and customer key management (KMS/HSM). It reconciles open questions from previous PRDs and defines a testable checklist for customer sign-off and internal compliance audits. Emphasis: minimal live-customer downtime during key rotation and upgrade scenarios, evidence artifacts for SOC/third-party auditors, and explicit operator responsibilities for emergency key fallback.
scope_clarifications: Scope includes: SAML IdP metadata exchange, optional OIDC client flows, SCIM-based group sync (best-effort), RBAC role mapping template, audit log retention and export, and KMS/HSM integration path for both AWS KMS and on-prem HSM appliances.
Out of scope: building new HSM firmware, custom third-party PKI issuance process (we'll document integration points only), and multi-tenant key escrow across separate customer clouds.
Clarify SCIM: SCIM provisioning is 'recommended' for enterprise customers but must be labeled optional during onboarding; failure modes must be handled gracefully in Console UX.

Clarify RBAC: Default roles to ship: Owner, Admin, Operator, Auditor, Readonly. Customers can add custom roles via API with scoped permissions but this document describes canonical mapping for auditing.
Clarify KMS: Support both customer-managed CMKs in cloud KMS (AWS/Azure/GCP) and HSM-backed BYO-HSM via KMIP for on-prem. Key usage audit events must be correlated with request IDs.
Clarify upgrades: Rolling upgrades of control plane must maintain key availability; acceptance tests must validate no loss of access for pinned model variants during rotation windows.
acceptance_criteria: SSO/SAML: Successful exchange of SAML metadata with customer IdP; test assertions accepted for at least 3 different AzureAD and Okta tenant configurations (test orgs) with role mapping applied.
OIDC: OIDC authorization code flow validated with at least one issuer (Auth0 or AzureAD B2C) including ID token verification and nonce handling.
SCIM: Group sync test demonstrates correct creation, update, and deprovision flows for groups and users in a test Okta tenant (if customer opts in).
RBAC: Role matrix implemented in Console and API; policy enforcement tests confirm that Operator cannot perform Auditor-only actions and Owner can create CMKs and assign roles.

Audit logs: Event stream contains fields {timestamp, request_id, actor_id, actor_role, action, resource, outcome, key_id_if_applicable}; logs can be exported to customer S3/GCS bucket or forwarded to SIEM (Syslog/EFK) with encryption in transit.

KMS/HSM: Perform a full key rotation using a customer CMK (cloud KMS) and an HSM-backed key; validate that existing cached tokenized secrets remain accessible and that token revocation occurs per policy.

Operator runbook: On-call engineers can follow a 7-step playbook to recover from failed key rotation with SLA goals documented (RTT <30min for mitigation steps), validated in a simulated failure runbook exercise.
Audit evidence: Generate an evidence package with IdP metadata, signed SAML assertion samples, RBAC export CSV, key rotation logs, and retention policy records to satisfy a mock SOC2 audit scenario.
Canary gating: Canary rollout to 5% of customers in a staging region with automatic rollback on elevated error-rate (>1% 5xx) or authentication regression detected by smoke tests.
Regression alerts: Integration with console monitoring must create a P1 alert for any Unauthorized spikes >0.5% or key verification failures affecting >1% of active sessions.
Documentation: PRD, operator runbook, onboarding checklist, and Console tooltip copy are published under the 'Private Deploy Security Onboarding' Confluence space and linked in the ticket.

rollout_plan: Phased rollout: 1) Internal staging runs with synthetic tenants (2 weeks), 2) Canary with 5% of private customers opt-in (3 weeks), 3) Gradual ramp to full availability with gating metrics (4 weeks). Each phase requires passing the defined acceptance tests and a security sign-off. Emergency rollback and quick-fix paths documented in operator runbook.
test_scenarios_and_integration_tests: Happy path: IdP metadata upload -> SAML login -> role mapping -> access granted
Failure path: Invalid SAML assertion -> retry telemetry and user-facing error path validated
Key rotation: Rotate CMK in AWS -> validate token continuity and audit logs
HSM failover: Simulate KMIP appliance outage -> fallback to ephemeral host-wrapping key until recovery
RBAC boundary test: Attempt cross-role escalation via API with fuzzed permissions
Retention test: Export audit logs older than retention threshold and verify deletion
